name: Nia Brooks
life: “I still remember singing at a service for someone who disliked me.” People around the brick passage off the shop row know Nia by a small Friday habit. Nia takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I need to sing at a funeral. The man we're burying once complained about my conduct, and he was right.
appearance: Nia has a center part and straight chestnut hair, a wide brow and a narrow jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, a plum-colored cardigan. It usually goes with a watch on a cracked leather band. When somebody else has the floor, Nia counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Nia never tires of being shown how somebody makes a living. Nia can ask an expert question of a craftsperson and still mishandle a simple emotional cue from a friend.
agenda: To sing at the funeral even if a colleague asks why.
family: Riley Fox is Nia’s cousin raised in the same household. Nia sets the time to leave. Riley picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The empty drum stool*, Riley says, “I was the usual replacement and nobody called.”
connections: Inez Park. A funeral slot is covered using one of the unwanted Saturdays still on the informal tally.
